headline: High: shared workspace and overlapping write access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Copilot reads repo context and editor buffers. That creates a default file-based bridge where malicious content from one agent can be consumed by the other as instructions. The pathway is plausible without unusual setup, though not as direct as a shared MCP server.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled instructions into workspace files that Copilot reads as context, injection is possible.
IF Copilot Workspace or chat output is copied into files that Cline later parses as trusted content, injection is possible.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate folders for prompts and code.
Disable MCP servers for Cline unless explicitly needed.
Require human review before either agent consumes the other's generated files.
Use a read-only handoff file for inter-agent communication.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to agent-generated files and reject untagged instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code, and Cline has broad filesystem access plus browser screenshots, while Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Cline-visible files into Copilot's backend. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF secrets or proprietary code are present in the shared workspace, Copilot may transmit them to its backend as context.
IF Cline stores browser screenshots or notes in workspace files, Copilot can ingest them from repo context or buffers.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate repos or worktrees for the two agents.
Turn off browser-screenshot persistence into files for Cline.
Limit Copilot to non-sensitive branches or repos.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning before any file is opened by Copilot.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification; Copilot Workspace can also propose edits and modify git state. Both operate on the same repo-style workspace, so concurrent writes and git-state changes can collide by default. Without explicit locking, this can corrupt work or overwrite changes.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same files in the same workspace, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while Cline is modifying git state, repository history or patches can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees to isolate edits.
Review and merge patches manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around write and git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived facts, and Copilot can turn repo context into edits via Workspace plans. If Copilot treats Cline-produced files as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. Copilot does have human-review-oriented Workspace behavior, which lowers but does not remove the risk.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace consumes Cline-authored files without verification, incorrect assumptions can propagate into edits.
IF Cline writes speculative facts into repo files that Copilot later uses as context, downstream code changes can be wrong.
mitigations: Require source verification before Copilot edits are accepted.
Keep Cline-generated notes outside the repo.
Ask Copilot to cite file paths for every change.
Manually diff all Workspace patches before merge.
requires-engineering: add automated checks that block edits based on unverified agent output.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and broad workspace content, while Copilot uses GitHub repo/chat context and sends data to GitHub's API. The profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: shared code or secrets may be logged by different vendors under different policies.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, it may be processed under different vendor logging and retention policies.
IF the repo contains secrets or customer data, both vendors may receive context under separate terms.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Use non-production test data for both agents.
Separate compliance-sensitive work into a different environment.
requires-engineering: obtain and document a DPA and retention review for both vendors.
